# Specifics

For a good overview of all the options, check out the [Authoring section in the Quarto docs, starting with markdown basics](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html).

## Metadata

Quarto uses the metadata specified in each `.qmd` file to format the page. For an overview, check out the [formats that are supported](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/all-formats.html), with specific focus on [the html format](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-basics.html). The default minimum metadata per page should be:


``` md         
---
title: "Style guide"
subtitle: "Overview of the principles and specific steps we use to make our material professional and consistent"
date: 2026-09-29
date-modified: last-modified
draft: true
---

# Text of article

```

-   `title` - states the (short) name of the page
-   `subtitle` - a summary of the page. Optional
-   `date`  - when the article was last published
-   `date-modified` - when the article was last updated. Note, for many pages, this is set at a hard coded date to start. However once you edit the page, please change this to a value of `last-modified`, which will make Quarto render it automatically to the date the specific `.qmd` file was changed.
-   `draft` - whether there is an orange draft header to the page or not. You can use this to publish draft pages for review (`draft: true`) before they are considered final (either set it as `draft: false` or remove the `draft` from the top of the `yaml`)

## Page overview

Each page should start with a sentence or two at the top introducing the metarial, then headings per topic, and sub-headings (h2) for sub-parts

## Links

There are many ways to [make links](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#links-images), depending on what you want to do. The default is:

``` md
See the [aggregation](/handbook/aggregation.qmd) section for more details.
```

Which will be rendered as:

> See the [aggregation](/handbook/aggregation.qmd) section for more details.

**Note**: You can specify the link relative to the root directory (hence `/handbook/...`) or relative to the folder the `qmd` file you are editing (hence you can state `aggregation.qmd` if say you are on the `glossary.qmd` file).

## Tables

There are [many ways](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/tables.html) to make tables. The minimum default is to separate the id of the table and to give it a title. That way you can reference the table in the text.

For example:

``` md
| fruit  | price  |
|:-------|--------|
| apple  | 2.05   |
| pear   | 1.37   |
| orange | 3.09   |

: Fruit prices {#tbl-fruits .striped .hover}

In the body of your text, you can reference the @tbl-fruits.
```

This will rendered as follows:

| fruit  | price |
|:-------|-------|
| apple  | 2.05  |
| pear   | 1.37  |
| orange | 3.09  |

: Fruit prices {#tbl-fruits .striped .hover}

In the body of your text, you can reference the @tbl-fruits.

## Figures

There are also a lot of ways to embed [figures](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/figures.html) into the text.

``` md
![The handbook logo](/handbook/images/logo.png){
    #fig-logo
    fig-align="center" 
    width=50%}

This is illustrated well by @fig-logo.
```

This will be rendered as:

![The handbook logo](/handbook/images/logo.png){
    #fig-logo
    fig-align="center" 
    width=50%}

This is illustrated well by @fig-logo.

## Callouts

[Callouts](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/callouts.html) can be used to call attention to specific types of things.
